newsitem.title: DUBAI: Cathay carries 10 T beans, fish ex-Dubai daily.
newsitem.headline: Cathay carries 10 T beans, fish ex-Dubai daily.

text.p: Cathay Pacific is carrying around 10 tonnes a day of fresh fish and green beans from the Arabian peninsula to Taiwan, United Arab Emirates cargo manager F.A. Baig said on Monday.

"We are carrying at least 10 tonnes a day of green beans and fresh fish from Oman and the UAE and are expecting 600-700 tonnes for the whole season until mid-March," he said, adding that the cargo is mostly destined for Taiwan.
But a ban on carrying perishable cargo on its new Boeing Co 777 aircraft is limiting the amount Cathay can carry.
"If this problem was solved my uplift could be multipied," he said, adding that three of the 15 weekly eastbound flights through Dubai were operated by 777s.
"We are not making full use of it because of these restrictions," he added.

In June, 306 passengers and 15 Cathay crew had to be evacuated on chutes at Hong Kong's airport after a smoke warning in the cargo hold. The false alarm is thought to have been triggered by a cargo of tightly-packed frogs, which caused a build up of condensation, setting off the fire sensor.
Boeing has said it has developed a cure for the 777 cargo smoke detection systems.
